reviews.title: Extremely Strict Rules and Disproportionate Penalties
reviews.body:
Every prop firm has its own rules, and I fully understand that traders are responsible for following them. However, my review is based on my personal experience with Dolvero and a comparison with an established, professional prop firm such as FTMO.

My experience with Dolvero has not been entirely satisfactory. The company has extremely strict rules regarding trading during high-impact economic news events (NEWS). I accidentally opened a trade 27 minutes before the end of the restricted 30-minute window, and my account was terminated. Customer support refused to reinstate it.

On another account, I had 9 BUY positions open, each with a volume of 0.1 lot, and accidentally opened one opposite SELL position of 0.1 lot. This was neither intentional hedging nor part of any trading strategy. Nevertheless, my account was immediately terminated, and customer support once again refused to reinstate it.

I acknowledge that both situations technically violated Dolvero's rules. However, when comparing Dolvero with FTMO, I believe there is a significant difference in their overall approach to traders, particularly in terms of risk management, the proportionality of penalties, and customer support.

I believe that a professional prop firm should not only strictly enforce its rules but also be able to distinguish between deliberate abuse of trading conditions and genuine human error.

My rating therefore primarily reflects a comparison of the quality of service and overall approach of FTMO and Dolvero, rather than simply my dissatisfaction with the termination of my accounts.

I recommend that traders carefully review all trading restrictions before purchasing a challenge.

replies.author: dolvero
replies.body:
Dušan, thank you for writing it in the open. Our reviews sit next to the account record, so let me put the record next to your words.

One thing your review leaves out: we did forgive you once. On 17 September your first account was flagged for hedging, 13 pairs. I read every one of your 41 trades myself, accepted that it was two mistaken clicks, restored the account personally, with its balance and trades intact, and wrote to you in black and white that hedging is not allowed and would not be forgiven a second time. So the distinction between abuse and human error that you ask for was made, in your favour, and you knew where the line was.

Since 15 September you have opened eight $100,000 evaluations with us, one of them free with a promotion. Seven have ended, and only two of them by the rules you describe as disproportionate. The other five ended on the risk limits every prop firm has: four on the daily loss limit (days of minus 5,600 to minus 6,000 USD), four on the 10% maximum drawdown (13.2%, 13.0%, 14.1% and 10.3%), three on the 2% risk-per-trade rule (single trades losing 6,480, 6,784, 12,713 and 12,912 USD) and two on weekend holding, with positions kept open for 10 and 13 days across weekends. Those are not technicalities.

Hedging, the second time. On 29 October it happened again, on the free account: not 9 buy positions but 17, 1.80 lots of gold open at once, and a sell opened from your phone against all of them. I do not doubt that it was unintentional. The rule you signed does not ask about intent, and the one exception had already been used, in writing.

News. The trade on 16 October was opened 24 minutes after the release and 6 minutes before the end of the window, not 27 minutes before the end. On 29 October we narrowed the news window to 10 minutes and to the currency of the release, for everyone, going forward, after feedback that included yours. No prop firm applies a new rule backwards, and neither do we.

You signed the trading rules fifteen times, once per account and once per new version, each time with a one-time code. Every breach has a published report with the full record, for instance dolvero.com/reviews/eval2610207103-hedging.html, and this review of yours is published with your account data beside it. I would welcome that comparison with any firm you name.

Your paid account EVAL2610202851 is active and in profit. You are still trading with us, and you are welcome to.

Michal Król, CEO

Michal Król, CEO

replies.body:
Thank you, Selinah. The alerts, the Discord and the fast answers are there on purpose, so it is good to hear they land.

On payouts on demand: I understand the wish, and the answer is no, for a reason that protects you. The first payout opens 14 days after the first trade and needs 10 profitable days, so what gets paid is trading, not one lucky afternoon. Once the window opens we are fast: the payouts we sent today left within hours of the request, one of them in eleven minutes after the identity check.

Your record is public next to this review, so I will say it plainly: your accounts so far have ended on the daily loss limit and the trailing drawdown, and three of them we replaced for free. LIVE2611025154 started today. Trade it smaller than you feel like, collect the ten days, and the first payout will be the one you are looking forward to. We will be here for it.

Michal Król, CEO

Thank you, Akhoy. One thing your review does not mention, probably because nobody tells traders this: your account survived its own payout.

When the 140.48 left, the profit was settled off the account, the balance went back to 5,000 and the history was archived, but the trailing floor stayed where your best day had put it, at 4,942.57. Most accounts cannot take that step. Yours did, with fifty-seven dollars to spare, and it is still trading a week later.

That is also why the next payout on this same account pays eighty percent, not seventy. The firm's share goes down each time an account proves it can be paid and keep going. You are the case the rule was written for.

Michal Król, CEO

Thank you, Adiar. Let me name the "issues regarding the rules", because they were not yours.

On 28 October at 01:36 UTC our news rule closed your account. It was the old rule, thirty minutes around any high-impact release on any instrument. You wrote to us at 02:19 and had an answer at 02:21. The next day the rule became what it should have been from the start, ten minutes and only the currency of the release, and your account came back with every trade on it.

So the quick responses are the part we can promise to keep up. The better part is that the rule itself got fixed, and your ticket was one of the reasons it did. You are up 244 dollars since then. Keep going.

Michal Król, CEO
